description: Customer reports repeated duplicate external tool invocations (webhook posts) tied to SDK reconnects. Problem appears when a client-side 'epoch shard' rotation interacts with our edge proxy frame splitting, resulting in a truncated idempotency key (trailing characters dropped). The shortened key collides with earlier in-flight requests and causes at-least-once delivery of downstream tool calls. This is urgent: ParcelFlow sees duplicate fulfillment jobs and billing impact. Customer is on Dedicated and has predictable capacity; impact is limited to a subset of long-running streamed requests that include tool/function calls.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use ParcelFlow's Go SDK with streaming function-calls enabled (long-running chat session, avg token window ~15k).
2) Configure client to rotate epoch shard identifier every 10 minutes (customer uses a custom shard UUID scheme).
3) Simulate an intermittent network hiccup that triggers reconnect + resume (common in their mobile fleet).
4) Observe that idempotency header (X-Redwood-Idempotency) is sent near end of an HTTP/2 frame and is split by the edge proxy; on reconnect the client resends a truncated header value (suffix lost).
5) Downstream webhook receives duplicated tool call POSTs (same semantics, different idempotency values after truncation) and side-effects fire twice.
logs: 2026-03-10T15:02:12Z edge-proxy: got request stream-id=0x7f2 headers: X-Redwood-Idempotency=9f3e1a8b... (frame-split=Y)
2026-03-10T15:02:12Z sdk-go(client): rotating shard epoch -> 0x4b9c; sending resume with idempotency=9f3e1a8b4b9c
2026-03-10T15:02:14Z edge-proxy: resume failed, reconstructed header truncated -> 9f3e1a8b4 (missing trailing 4b9c)
2026-03-10T15:02:14Z serving-runtime: accepted request id=9f3e1a8b4 and triggered funcall tool_id=fetch-ratecheck, webhook POST 200
2026-03-10T15:02:16Z serving-runtime: another request accepted id=9f3e1a8b4b9c (original complete key) and triggered funcall tool_id=fetch-ratecheck, webhook POST 200
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: client-side epoch rotation algorithm appends shard suffix without stable normalization; when header is split across HTTP/2 frames the proxy concatenation drops trailing frame bytes under high concurrency.

Hypothesis B: edge-proxy had an earlier mitigation that trims header values longer than 64 bytes; combined with shard suffix increase the key crosses the threshold and proxy returns a truncated symbol without warning.

Repro on staging: replicated with local proxy + controlled HTTP/2 frame split. When we force header chunking at the same boundary as customer reported rotation timing, proxy concatenation logic returned a different assembled header in ~72% of trials.

Telemetry: only hits for long-lived streaming sessions (>5m) and clients that rotate shard epoch more frequently than 30m. Metric: downstream duplicate-webhook-rate spiked to 0.7% for ParcelFlow between 2026-03-09T22:00 and 2026-03-10T02:00 UTC.

Edge-proxy code path: headerReassemble() currently uses a byte-buffer with maxLen=128 and a trimming pass that ran before we deployed binary-compat safety in v1.14. The trim is applied if buffer contains non-printable bytes; rotation suffix introduced non-ASCII padding in one customer's implementation (base64-url variant with no padding).
comments: 2026-03-10 Alyssa Chen (Support): Initial triage and customer impact notes. Asked customer for sample server logs, SDK config, and proxy topology. Added 'investigation' tag.

2026-03-11 Ravi Patel (SRE): Reproduced locally by forcing HTTP/2 frame split at header boundary. Confirmed concatenation bug where trailing fragment dropped when client sent header across multiple frames and the buffer trim path executed. Created reproducer gist and linked PR candidate.

2026-03-12 ParcelFlow Ops (customer): Provided production trace IDs and SDK config showing their custom epoch-shard suffix generator. Note: they intentionally omit base64 padding under constraints of legacy datastore keys.

2026-03-13 Ravi Patel (SRE): Patch prepared to skip trim for headers named X-Redwood-Idempotency and to accept base64-url unpadded values. Running canary in staging-edge; observed no duplicate-replay across 10k simulated reconnects.

2026-03-14 Alyssa Chen (Support): Sent interim mitigation guidance to customer: recommend disabling epoch-shard rotation until patch, or change generator to include stable padding (use RFC4648 base64 with padding) as a temporary workaround. Customer acknowledged and requested expedited fix for Dedicated fleet.
resolution: Patch merged to edge-proxy to preserve contiguous header bytes for X-Redwood-Idempotency and to accept base64-url unpadded values without trimming. Deployed canary to us-east edge nodes 2026-03-14 04:00 UTC, followed by full rollout 2026-03-14 10:00 UTC. Customer switched to temporary mitigation (stop shard rotation) on 2026-03-13 and reports no further duplicate tool side-effects. Follow-up: create an SDK note recommending stable idempotency key encoding and add a test in edge-proxy integration suite for header chunk reassembly. Keeping ticket open until 2026-03-20 for post-rollout validation.
postmortem_action_items: 1) Add integration test in CI that simulates HTTP/2 header chunking and validates idempotency header reassembly (owner: edge-proxy).
2) Add validation/error telemetry when reconstructed idempotency key length < expected (owner: telemetry).
3) Update SDK docs with recommended key canonicalization (RFC4648, include padding) and runtime guardrail to warn when key contains non-printable bytes (owner: SDK docs).
4) Ops: schedule dedicated fleet sweep for duplicate-delivery alert during the rollback window on 2026-03-14 (owner: support-ops).
